about: Release Tracker app catalog. Edit freely: add an object to 'apps' to offer a new app in the App Catalog tab. Fields: name, category, description, url, source_mode (auto|web|direct — web = scan a download page for links, direct = a 'latest' link that redirects to the newest file), asset_pattern ({version} = version number, * = wildcard), install_type (auto|archive|copy|sfx|mozilla|inno|installer|msi), install_mode (merge|clean), strip_mode (auto|always|never), protect (; separated), exe_name, installer_args ({dest} = install folder), folder (sub-folder under the global destination), auto_pick (true = if the pattern finds nothing, pick the best Windows x64 file automatically), notes. Apps are always shown in alphabetical order. Extra fields: version_regex (regex with one group that reads the version from the download page when the file name has none), file_hint (web pages: auto-picked files must start with this), pick (web pages: 'first' = take the first matching link instead of the highest version). Link fields: link_text (regex for the VISIBLE text of the download link, for pages whose links have no file name), link_context (regex that must appear just before that link, e.g. '64-bit'). rev: raise it when you fix an entry; already-tracked copies of that app are reset and re-installed cleanly. verified: false = entry written from knowledge of the project, not yet confirmed against a live release; run Fetch Assets once (auto_pick fixes most wrong guesses). Icon fields: icon (optional path to a .png or .ico shown for the app before it has been downloaded; relative paths are relative to the program folder) and exe_hint (optional file-name pattern of the app's main program inside its download, e.g. 'gfie.exe', used to pick the right program when reading the icon). Normally both stay empty: the icon is read from the program itself after it has been downloaded or installed. Version-page sources (source_mode 'template', for sites that hide their download links behind JavaScript): url = a plain page that names the newest version, version_regex = regex with ONE group that reads version numbers from that page's text (the highest one wins), download_url = the file's address with {version} ({version_nodots} = 3711, {version_underscore} = 3_71_1). If the newest version's file isn't online yet, the next version is tried. PortableApps.com packages (*.paf.exe) are unpacked with 7-Zip (install_type 'sfx') and started through their launcher. Installer-only apps (no zip): set install_type 'installer' and installer_args (use {dest} for the install folder) and the tracker runs the vendor's installer for you. Prefer switches that only COPY files into {dest} — Bitvise (-extract=y), Opera (--copyonly=1 --singleprofile=1), calibre Portable — over a normal silent install (NSIS: /S /D=, Inno Setup: /VERYSILENT /DIR=): a normal install may write to the registry and other folders, which the tracker cannot undo, and installer entries get no backups or roll back. exe_hint names the program the Run button should start. download_url may use {version}, {version_nodots} or {version_underscore}. Check fields (written by catalog_check.py when you click 'Apply results'): last_check (date), check_result (ok | warn | fail) and check_note (why). verified = true only when the last check passed. Mozilla installers (Thunderbird / Firefox Setup *.exe): install_type 'mozilla' unpacks the installer with 7-Zip, keeps only its 'core' folder as the install folder, creates a Data\profile folder and switches off the app's own updater with a policy file. run_args (optional) = arguments the Run button and shortcuts pass to the program, {dest} = install folder, e.g. -profile "{dest}\Data\profile" -no-remote. {dest_url} (in run_args) = the install folder written for a file:/// address, e.g. LibreOffice: -env:UserInstallation=file:///{dest_url}/Data/profile. Single-file apps whose file name has no version (AnyDesk.exe): use source_mode 'template' with a plain page that names the version and put '#{version}' at the end of download_url — the part after '#' is never sent to the server. Inno Setup installers (install_type 'inno'): unpacked with innounp (path set in Settings → Options), never run — nothing is installed. Only the installer's {app} files are kept, so any shortcuts, registry entries and run-time tasks the installer would have made are skipped. strip_mode 'always' unwraps a single top folder; otherwise the files go in as they are. Needs an innounp new enough for the installer's Inno Setup version. innounp versions: the original innounp 0.50 reads Inno Setup only up to 6.1.2; installers made after 2022 usually need innounp-2 (the Unicode build by J. Rathlev, reads up to Inno Setup 7.1). When innounp fails, Release Tracker's error names the Inno Setup version that made the installer. marker_files (optional; ';' separated; a trailing '/' means a folder): empty files / folders created next to the app's program after every install or update, if they are missing — e.g. 'portable.txt' (Dolphin, DuckStation), 'portable.ini' (PCSX2), 'emu.cfg' (Flycast), 'user/' (Azahar). They are what switches those apps to keeping their settings beside the program; existing ones are never touched and are protected from a clean update.
